statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases from 25 to 21 because the declared closing-auction window passed without a directional close: the Nasdaq-100 finished at 29,077.22, 124 points above the 28,953.26 low it had broken and reclaimed. Index futures are now inside the daily 21:00-22:00 UTC CME halt, so the 22:00 UTC reopen is the declared danger window.
recommendation: The cash Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,077.22, -379.75 points and -1.29% against a 29,456.97 previous close, inside a 28,953.26 to 29,267.42 day range. The session low broke during the 19:00 UTC hour on fresh U.S. strikes and was reclaimed before the close, so the breakdown failed rather than extended. CME index futures last traded 29,139.00 before the 21:00 UTC maintenance halt and reopen at 22:00 UTC. Mapped policy state: WATCH, with the danger window placed on the 22:00-23:00 UTC futures reopen rather than on the current halted hour.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closes at 29,077 with the failed breakdown intact, but Iran strikes U.S. regional bases and a ceasefire is ruled out while index futures sit in their daily halt
body:
The structural fact of this hour is that the U.S. cash session ended without confirming the escalation. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,077.22, down 1.29%, which is 124 points above the 28,953.26 low set during the 19:00 UTC hour and roughly in the middle of the 28,953.26 to 29,267.42 day range. A session-extreme break that is reclaimed and then closed away from is a failed breakdown, and it is the fourth clear retracement the index offered on a day that opened into a geopolitical shock. That is the opposite of the no-retracement path that would threaten a mean-reversion approach. The S&P 500 closed -0.71% at 7,631.47 and the Nasdaq Composite -1.03% at 26,099.77, so the decline was orderly and broad rather than a disorderly index-level break.

Against that, the news flow deteriorated after the close. Iranian state media described a decisive operation against U.S. bases and interests in the region from roughly 18:45 UTC, alarm sirens were reported in Jordan's Mafraq and Aqaba governorates around 20:35 UTC, and around 20:43 UTC the prospect of ceasefire negotiations was publicly dismissed while a much larger response was threatened. Two civilians were reported killed in the earlier U.S. strikes. This is an active, two-sided military exchange with no de-escalation signal at the assessment cutoff.

What separates those two facts is venue. CME index futures entered their daily maintenance halt at 21:00 UTC, last trading 29,139.00 against a 29,002.00 to 29,571.25 session range, and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC. For the current clock-hour there is no price path in which a pathological structure could form, which is why Tail steps down to 21 rather than holding the elevated band. Tail does not fall further because the same halt is accumulating headlines that will be priced in a single reopen print, and because the energy channel is still extending: WTI is $90.68, +5.74%, after a $90.97 day high, and Brent is $95.22 after a $95.41 high, both set after the equity close.

Stress is 76, high band. The 10-year yield is 4.796% against a 4.800% day high, its highest since January 2025, inside a global long-end selloff, and VIX closed 16.34, +9.52%. The notable feature is the absolute level of volatility: 16.34 is a modest reading for a day carrying an active military exchange and a five percent crude move, which argues that the equity market is pricing an energy and rates transmission rather than a systemic event.

Confidence is 82, down from 89. Index, volatility, crude, Brent and 10-year levels were read directly from primary quote pages after the close, and the escalation timeline was verified against two independent live-coverage sources. The reduction is specific and honest: with futures halted there is no live price-path evidence for the current hour, and the shared Finviz cross-asset context was 153 minutes old at assessment time, therefore stale under the inherited freshness rule, and was not used as current evidence.

The declared danger window is 22:00-23:00 UTC, the Globex reopen. That single hour is where an hour of accumulated escalation headlines meets the thinnest liquidity of the day, and it is the narrowest window that covers the actual risk. A reopen that holds above the 29,002.00 futures low would confirm the decay path; a reopen that gaps through it and extends would be the first genuine evidence of the one-way structure that has been absent all session.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-two of the 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment; the 15:00 and 20:00 UTC hours on 1 September have none and are marked unavailable. The first eleven slots, covering the late 31 August U.S. session and the overnight hours into 1 September, all sat in the EA_ON band with Tail between 9 and 12 and mode mixed, while Stress drifted from 52 down to 50 and then up to 58 as crude firmed and long yields climbed. The regime broke at 08:00 UTC, when the Hormuz escalation pushed Tail to 22 and mode to trend-down; Tail then held the 25-31 orange band from 09:00 to 13:00 UTC, peaking at 31 with Stress 75 around the U.S. cash open. From 14:00 UTC a genuine retracement developed and mode moved to event/whipsaw: Tail fell to 24, then 21 at 16:00 UTC, before settling at 24 and 23 across 17:00 and 18:00 UTC. The final published hour, 19:00 UTC, returned to 25 and BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES as a fresh strike wave broke the session low inside the closing auction. Across the whole window the index repeatedly offered two-way trade rather than compounding into a single one-way path, and Stress rose steadily from 52 to 77 while Tail never left a 9 to 31 range.
outlookSummary: The projection opens at 21 for the current 21:00 UTC hour, inside the CME maintenance halt where no price path can form, then peaks at 24 for the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, the single declared danger window, where an hour of accumulated escalation headlines meets the thinnest liquidity of the day and the 29,002.00 futures low is the named reference. It steps down to 22 and 20 across the first two post-reopen hours on the assumption that discovery is orderly and two-way, decays to a conditional overnight floor of 16 from 04:00 to 06:00 UTC, and lifts modestly to 17-18 through the European session as the Bund and gilt long ends reopen into the same global yield pressure. Risk rises again on 2 September: 19 into the 12:15 UTC ADP release, 20 across the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open, and a second-day peak of 21 in the 14:00 UTC hour, which carries Factory Orders and the 14:30 UTC EIA crude inventory print directly into a live energy shock. It eases to 17-19 into the 2 September close. Every reading after the current hour is conditional risk, not observed structure. Confidence decays from 82 to 50 across the horizon, and Stress follows the same arc while staying in the elevated-to-high bands throughout, because crude, the long end and the Hormuz situation are all unresolved at the cutoff.
